- Short-latency / dense-cut guidance: do not avoid a single high-contradiction boundary by picking adjacent splits that fragment noun phrases, reduced relatives, or enumerations. In ≤3–≤5 regimes prefer earlier cuts that land at natural NP or list boundaries (or just before coordinating conjunctions) so reference and enumerations stay intact. Also ensure predicate completion: keep verbs with their required objects/complements and delay a cut if the verb phrase is incomplete.

- Predicate completion: avoid cutting between a verb/predicate and its core arguments or complements. If the verb or a required object may appear after a candidate cut, delay the cut until the verb phrase and its obligatory complements are present.
